extracted.intended_audience: Congressional staff, regulators (EPA/CARB/DOJ), policymakers, journalists, and the public following the Volkswagen emissions investigation
extracted.subtask_description: Transcript of a Congressional subcommittee investigative hearing into Volkswagen's use of software that circumvents emissions controls, EPA/CARB testing and enforcement responses, and questions about recalls and fixes. Contains factual findings, regulatory standards, investigatory steps, and procedural obligations discussed by witnesses and members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and prohibition of a 'defeat device'
rubrics_metrics.description: Software installed in the electronic control module that senses when the vehicle is being tested for compliance with EPA emissions standards and changes operation so emissions controls are reduced or turned off during normal driving but enabled during official emissions tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transcript explains: 'these cars contain software that turns off or significantly reduces the effectiveness of emissions controls when driving normally and turns them on when the car is undergoing an official emissions test.' It lists inputs used to sense testing (steering wheel position, vehicle speed, duration of engine operation, barometric pressure). Such devices result in emissions far above allowable standards (up to 40 times in the example) and are illegal under the Clean Air Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for EPA Certificate of Conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: All new cars sold in the United States must have an EPA-issued Certificate of Conformity demonstrating that the car meets applicable federal emissions standards to control air pollution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturing or selling vehicles that do not conform to the certificate (e.g., due to defeat devices enabling higher real-world emissions) violates federal requirements. This is presented as a basic statutory prerequisite for lawful sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for making/selling vehicles with defeat devices and for concealment
rubrics_metrics.description: Making and selling vehicles with defeat devices that allow emissions higher than certified violates multiple Clean Air Act provisions; concealing the facts from EPA, the State of California, and consumers compounds the seriousness of the violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transcript states violations are 'very serious not only because the illegal defeat device results in excess emissions many times the allowable standard, but also because, after the high emissions were discovered, VW concealed the facts from EPA, the State of California, and from consumers.' Concealment affects enforcement posture and potential remedies/penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement assessment criteria (scope, additional vehicles, economic benefit, penalties, excess pollution, mitigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA intends to assess: the scope of the company's liability under the Clean Air Act; whether additional vehicles contain defeat devices; the economic benefit to the company from non-compliance; appropriate penalties; the excess pollution resulting from violations; and appropriate ways to mitigate excess pollution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the metrics EPA will use during its ongoing investigation and in determining remedies and penalties. The transcript notes coordination with DOJ on such assessments and that release of certain investigative details may be limited to avoid jeopardizing the investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness requirement for recall fixes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recall remedies proposed by the manufacturer must effectively address the excess emissions and bring vehicles into compliance; proposed fixes are to be tested (e.g., by CARB) to confirm effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: VW's December 2014 voluntary recall implemented software fixes; CARB testing later showed that those fixes were not effective. EPA directed VW to present more than one option on how to address the excess emissions and to allow testing of those options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to propose multiple remedy options and assess owner impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The manufacturer is to present more than one option for addressing excess emissions, and regulators will evaluate the options carefully, particularly regarding impacts on vehicle owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA/California directed VW to present multiple options and indicated they would 'look at these options very carefully, particularly with respect to what impacts they will have on the owners.' Timeliness and effectiveness are emphasized, but rushed fixes that are ineffective are cautioned against.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing program standards: lab testing, in-use testing, and on-road measurements; unpredictability
rubrics_metrics.description: Robust compliance and oversight require a combination of testing of new vehicles in the lab, testing of in-use vehicles in the lab, and on-road measurements; testing programs should be unpredictable to deter and detect defeat strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transcript states: 'what is required for a robust compliance and oversight program is both testing of new vehicles in the lab, testing of what we call in-use vehicles in the lab as on-road measurements' and that EPA will 'be unpredictable' in testing going forward in response to the episode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of effects of fixes on engine performance, fuel economy, and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating possible fixes, agencies will consider whether software or engineering solutions meaningfully degrade engine performance, reduce fuel economy, or create safety issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members raised concerns that fixes to meet emissions could 'hurt the vehicles' performance in other ways.' EPA stated it is asking VW technical questions about whether changing calibrations or software to maintain low-emission mode in normal driving would 'damage the engine or reduce power significantly,' and that answers depend on engine generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility varies by vehicle generation; older vehicles may require structural changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Feasibility of bringing vehicles into compliance varies by model/generation: newer generation diesel engines (Generation 3) may be easier to fix, whereas older models (2009–2014) that lack urea (SCR) systems may require more substantial engineering solutions such as installing urea systems or different NOx filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transcript explains the distinction and that 'the Generation 3 engines will be much easier to fix' but older vehicles 'will require a more substantial engineering solution' and that fixes could be 'quite elaborate.' Regulators expect VW to present viable options for each generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency coordination and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will work closely with the California Air Resources Board (CARB) and the U.S. Department of Justice during the investigation and enforcement process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CARB led much of the technical testing and contributed significantly to detecting and characterizing the problem. EPA will continue close coordination and referenced prior examples where either state or EPA took the lead depending on the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and document production to regulators, committees, and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: The company is expected to provide documents, communications, and explanations to regulators, to Congressional committees upon request, and to consumers explaining recalls and why they are necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the transcript: requests that VW provide the documents showing what explanations were given to consumers and regulators about the December 2014 recall, and a committee request for identification of who at VW participated in communications. EPA also provided FAQs for consumers (e.g., are cars safe to drive?).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptive oversight: update testing and enforcement approaches as technologies change
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory agencies must continuously update and adapt compliance oversight and testing approaches as vehicle technologies and circumstances change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA stated that over the 40-plus year history of the program they have 'continuously updated and adapted our approaches to compliance oversight as technologies and situations have changed,' and that lessons from this episode are being applied to step up testing activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal/procedural protections and limits on disclosure during active investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: During an ongoing enforcement investigation, certain information may be withheld to avoid jeopardizing the investigation; EPA coordinates with DOJ and follows investigative/prosecutorial norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Grundler stated they are 'unable to provide further details of the investigation because the release of such information could jeopardize this ongoing enforcement investigation' and that they will work closely with DOJ in assessment of penalties and remedies.
